commons.signatureFailed: SIGNATURE DID NOT VERIFY — do not rely on this
commons.weightNotAsserted: This publisher did not state how confident they are. The number below is computed from the facts above, and you can compute it yourself.
commons.noWeightShown: No weight is shown. Every input to the calculation — the source count, the observation window, the timing precision — lives in the same signed payload that failed verification. Deriving a number from data an attacker could have written, and printing it next to a warning, would give a false claim the appearance of measurement. There is nothing here to weigh.
commons.signatureIs: The signature is ML-DSA-65 over a SHA-256 digest of the claim.
commons.fingerprintsPublished: {count} input fingerprint(s) are published. Hash your own evidence the same way to see how much of it you already hold.
commons.sourcesNotPublished: Source identities are not published, by design — only a count.
commons.author: Author
commons.footer: Published as an attested claim. Weight, where shown, is derived from the stated method, not asserted by the publisher — the inputs are listed so you can check it.
commons.censusExplain: this is a count of every entry within a stated boundary, not an agreement between sources. Nothing here rests on a second opinion, and a second opinion about a register would be less authoritative than the register itself.
commons.precisionNotApplicableCensus: not applicable: no time window was used
commons.precisionNotApplicableEquality: not applicable: matched on an exact identifier, not a time window
commons.precisionWindow: how well the timing supports the claimed window
commons.recencyFromSnapshot: measured from the snapshot date, not from the publication date
commons.relayedExplain: , all relayed via {relays} — sources sharing one delivery path are discounted, because that path is a single point of failure the count cannot express
commons.setCommitmentHow: SHA-256 of the counted members, sorted and joined by newlines. The members themselves are not published; if you hold the same boundary, recompute this and compare.
